sources.citation: Tun, Maung Maung. 2014. A sociolinguistic survey of selected Bisoid varieties: Pyen, Laomian and Laopin. MA thesis, Payap University. 301 pp.
sources.note: Literature review only (pp.11-13): lists Cauho as its own lexicostatistic cluster after Kitjapol 2006 and cites Wright 1998b ms 'Phonological sketches of Phu Noi varieties of Phongsali Province'; no Cauho data, no stress statement.

sources.citation: Kitjapol Udomkool. 2006. A phonological comparison of selected Bisoid speech varieties. MA thesis, Payap University, Chiang Mai. xx+207 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 3.3 'Cauho' (pp. 91-114) gives syllable types CV/CVC/CVV/CVVC, 26 consonants, 9 vowels, diphthongs and four tones (35, 315, 33, 31; p.112) with tone distribution by initial/medial/final syllable (pp.113-114); sec. 4.1 (p.137): 'Tone is required on all syllables.' No mention of stress, accent or prominence anywhere in the 207 pp. (a full-text search for stress/accent). Data source: Sue Wright's recorded Cauho wordlist, retranscribed by the author (p.35).

sources.citation: Bradley, David. 1977. Phunoi or Côông. Papers in South East Asian Linguistics 5 (Pacific Linguistics A-49): 67-98.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in
sources.note: Describes Phunoi proper (phun1245), not Cauho; p.73 notes reduced minor syllables as first elements of compounds; no word-stress rule. Context only.
Cites only Udomkool 2006 and Wright n.d; autonym cau33 ho33; nothing on stress.
